summary:
ORBITX is an interactive 3D space mission simulation platform inspired by NASA's General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT). The project aims to provide an educational and realistic space exploration experience where users can take the role of spacecraft mission controllers.

Users can design and configure spacecraft, explore an interactive 3D solar system, select planets as destinations, plan orbital trajectories, and perform simplified space manoeuvres. The simulator includes different missions, such as Earth satellite deployment, Moon exploration, Mars exploration, geostationary satellite placement, and deep-space exploration.

The platform uses Three.js to create realistic 3D planetary environments and spacecraft animations. It also provides a mission-control dashboard that displays important flight information, including spacecraft velocity, orbital altitude, remaining fuel, distance to destination, and mission elapsed time.

ORBITX combines space science, physics, programming, and interactive gaming to help users understand orbital mechanics, spacecraft navigation, and space mission planning through practical simulation.

Main Technologies:
- HTML, CSS and JavaScript
- Three.js for 3D visualization
- React for the application interface
- Chart.js for data visualization
Project Goal:

To develop an engaging educational space simulator that makes complex space mission concepts easier to understand through interactive 3D exploration, spacecraft control.
details:
1. What is ORBITX?

ORBITX is an interactive 3D space mission simulator designed to help users understand how real space missions work.

It is inspired by NASA's General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT). The project allows users to experience the role of a space mission controller by selecting missions, configuring spacecraft, exploring planets, and simulating spacecraft journeys through space.

Instead of only reading about space exploration, users can interact with a virtual solar system and observe how spacecraft travel between different destinations.

2. What is the main purpose?

The main purpose of ORBITX is to make space science and orbital mechanics easier to understand through an interactive learning experience.

It helps users learn:

  • How spacecraft are launched into space.
  • How satellites move around Earth.
  • How spacecraft travel towards the Moon and other planets.
  • How fuel and propulsion affect a mission.
  • How orbital trajectories and course corrections work.
  • How mission controllers monitor spacecraft.
dataRefs: GMAT is an open-source, enterprise-level software system developed to support the design, analysis, optimisation, and navigation of space missions. Developed through collaboration involving NASA, private industry, academia, and other contributors, GMAT provides a comprehensive environment for modelling and analysing spacecraft trajectories across a wide range of mission scenarios. These include low Earth orbit, geostationary and highly elliptical orbits, lunar missions, libration-point trajectories, interplanetary transfers, and deep-space exploration.  GMAT enables users to model spacecraft, propulsion systems, trajectories, manoeuvres, and other mission components using high-fidelity physical models. It can be used for orbit propagation, trajectory optimisation, orbit determination, navigation-data simulation, launch-window analysis, manoeuvre planning, and the evaluation of different mission scenarios and engineering trade-offs.
